sources.title: District Gujranwala: Decline of the Mughal Empire
sources.scope: Retrospective district account, consulted 2026-09-28. Contains evaluative wording and conflicting dates; not a contemporary 1792 register.

sources.title: The Sikh Encyclopedia: Pattidari
sources.scope: Online secondary account citing H.T. Prinsep (1834) and Indu Banga. Only opening Sikh-period tenure discussion used; later southeast-Punjab statistics excluded.

sources.title: District Gujranwala: Sikh Administration under Ranjit Singh
sources.scope: Describes subsequent consolidated rule. Not a direct description of the child protagonist's authority or a 1792 taxation schedule.

sources.title: District Gujranwala: Geography
sources.scope: Present-day geographical orientation only; administrative extents not treated as historical Misl borders.

claims.statement: The district account describes Gujranwala as the headquarters of Charat Singh, Maha Singh and Ranjit Singh before Lahore.
claims.limit: It supplies context, not a measured city plan. Its Charat Singh dates conflict internally (1773/1778); its Maha Singh death date differs from the existing fixed 1792 game chronology. No automatic chronology changes or adopted moral characterizations.

claims.statement: The opening account distinguishes shared holdings and shares assigned among participating leaders and followers.
claims.limit: This motivates separate person, household, service and land relations. It does not establish particular rights, payments or quotas for these fictional Gujranwala requests.

claims.statement: The later administrative account distinguishes directly managed lands, contracted collections and jagirs associated with military or other service.
claims.limit: Those later structures are not transplanted wholesale into 1792. The game does not implement revenue farms, title grants or historical taxation percentages.

claims.statement: The present district geography places the Chenab to the north and describes neighbouring districts.
claims.limit: Local market and well coordinates remain authored in the inherited 56-metre test cell, not distant historical places or Misl borders.

nodes.label: One reserved hired guard; authored local detail

limits: The two requests, the speakers, appointment, costs and timing are original game design, not recorded incidents or reconstructed muster rolls.
One guard is reserved from existing hires. No extra population, garrison, treasury, revenue, land title or regional conquest is created.
Person, kinship, household service and Misl allegiance are not interchangeable. Existing Raj Kaur/Phulkian and other character records are untouched.
No borders, ranks, headcounts, equipment rosters or all-Punjab political organization are inferred from this local prototype.
